description.value: Ruckle Provincial Park occupies the southeastern tip of Salt Spring Island, offering tent camping in open grassy meadows overlooking Swanson Channel where ferries and pleasure craft pass in a steady parade. With seven kilometres of rocky shoreline, the park is one of the most biodiverse in the southern Gulf Islands, drawing wildlife watchers, scuba divers, and beachcombers to its tidal pools and coastal trails. For touring cyclists arriving by BC Ferries, it is a short ride from the Fulford Harbour terminal to one of the most scenic campgrounds in the region.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The official BC Parks page at bcparks.ca/ruckle-park/ confirms this is a real, active provincial park on Salt Spring Island offering frontcountry tent camping in grassy meadows. The site explicitly mentions a seasonal water system ('shut down for winter between November 1 and March 15'), confirming potable water exists when operational. The frontcountry and group camping subpages confirm reservations are accepted via camping.bcparks.ca; no other specific amenities (showers, toilets, hiker/biker sites, etc.) are mentioned in the fetched content, so those remain null.
concerns: OSM community field lists 'Sidney' but Ruckle Provincial Park is on Salt Spring Island, not in Sidney — these are distinct communities; may indicate a data entry error in the OSM record.

enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Ruckle Provincial Park is a real, active, publicly accessible BC Parks campground with a functioning website and confirmed reservations — a natural stop for touring cyclists on Salt Spring Island.
